principles.statement: A first-token command allowlist is not a security boundary: any allowlisted interpreter or runner (node, python3, find, git, npm, systemctl) can execute arbitrary code or change state through arguments.
principles.rationale: Found and fixed 2026-10-29 in terminal-mcp: node -e, python3 -c, find -exec/-delete, git -c/config, npm exec and systemctl restart all passed the old check while ; | & $ were blocked. Per-command argument denies now refuse them; 18/18 selftest. Residual by design: running a script file in the repo.

heuristics.name: Adding a command to an allowlist
heuristics.description: Enumerate its code-execution and state-changing flags/subcommands and deny them in the same change; add a selftest case per bypass class.
heuristics.when_to_apply: Every allowlist: terminal-mcp roles, android shell allowlist, any future shell-like tool.

decision_rules.condition: A command can run arbitrary code via its arguments
decision_rules.action: Deny the flag/subcommand, return success:false with the reason in an HTTP 200 body, and prefer a script file inside the repo.
